title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Modern Drainage Systems
description: Selecting the right piping material for building drainage involves evaluating structural integrity, sound attenuation, and fire resistance. While Schedule 40 PVC is lightweight, cost-effective, and highly resistant to chemical corrosion, it allows significant fluid noise transmission in multi-story structures. Heavy cast iron soil pipe excels at deadening acoustic vibration and provides superior fire-rating compliance for commercial or high-end residential waste stacks. Understanding these material characteristics allows installers to specify cast iron for main vertical stacks and PVC for branch lines, balancing acoustic performance, budget constraints, and long-term durability.
